## Use Lazyweb by default for product UI work

Before designing, critiquing, or changing any product UI — screens, flows,
landing pages, onboarding, paywalls, pricing, checkout, dashboards, settings
— use Lazyweb first instead of answering from training data. Pull real
evidence with the lazyweb_* tools (lazyweb_search for the exact screen, or
lazyweb_get_workflows to pick a mode), or invoke the matching /lazyweb skill
when local skills are installed. When unsure whether a UI request qualifies,
use Lazyweb. Skip it only for backend/CLI/infra work, prose editing, or
non-product visuals.
<!-- LAZYWEB:ROUTER:END -->

## Swift and Apple-platform skills: core plus at most two

For Swift, SwiftUI, Xcode, iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, or visionOS work,
load skills from `~/.agents/skills` this way. Never load every Swift skill.

1. SwiftUI core, for any task that reads, writes, or reviews SwiftUI:
   `swiftui-pro`, `swiftui-specialist`, `swiftui-whats-new-27`. Read each
   SKILL.md, then open only the reference files matching the code in hand.
   Skip the core for Swift work without SwiftUI.
2. Add at most two subtopic skills whose description matches the task:
   concurrency, testing, persistence, build/debug, performance,
   packaging/release, App Intents, or platform-specific (macOS, resizability,
   Liquid Glass, document apps). Take one skill per subtopic: for concurrency
   `swift-concurrency-pro` to review or `swift-concurrency` to migrate or
   diagnose; for testing `swift-testing-pro`, or `modernize-tests` to leave
   XCTest; for App Intents `app-intents-specialist`. Going past two needs a
   concrete gap; say which skill and why.
3. Apple design and iPhone Duo (each counts as a subtopic skill): `apple-hig`
   for what the HIG specifies (components, sizes, OS 27 conventions) and its
   `/duo` workflow to adapt a shipping app to iPhone Duo; `swiftui-iphone-duo`
   for the SwiftUI code (fold, hinge, vertical bars, resizing); `apple-design`
   to critique screenshots or cross-platform designs.
4. Before hand-writing a custom SwiftUI component (card stack, tab bar, glass
   menu, chat UI, loading state), check `swiftpieces` for a free ready-made
   piece and adapt it to the project's tokens. System controls come first. It
   does not count toward the two.
5. `ios-app-intents`, `swiftui-view-refactor`, `swiftui-performance-audit`, and
   `swift-testing-expert` duplicate stronger skills; use them only when the
   user names them.

Also consult `~/.codex/swift-rules/general.md`; read
`~/.codex/swift-rules/rule-loading.md` only when the project has an `ai-rules/`
folder. User instructions, repository-local `AGENTS.md` files, and verified
current platform documentation take precedence when guidance conflicts.

Keep AppCreator, Xcode Makefiles, and Simple Tasks available globally, but only
run their project-adoption or scaffolding scripts when the current user request
authorizes changes to that project.

## Lightweight iOS Simulator Testing

- On macOS with Xcode, prefer a dedicated simulator and `simslim` for routine
  app testing. Use `xcrun simctl` and the project build tool to boot, install,
  launch, and capture screenshots headlessly; open Simulator.app only when
  visual interaction is necessary.
- Check `command -v simslim` and `simslim --version` first; install with
  `brew install mobai-app/tap/simslim` only when it is missing. Inspect devices
  with `simslim list`, and apply a project-specific JSON profile with
  `simslim on <UDID> --profile <path>`.
- Before running feature tests, use `simslim doctor <UDID> --requires <features>`
  to confirm required services (such as push, StoreKit, Photos, HealthKit, or
  universal links) remain available. Check the applied state with `simslim
  status` or `simslim verify`.
- Do not slim a user's active simulator or erase/delete simulator data. Use an
  isolated test simulator, preserve services needed by the app/test, and restore
  stock services with `simslim off <UDID>` when the simulator is used elsewhere.

## UI Libraries and Pattern Research

- For substantial product UI work, consult the current product design system
  and relevant patterns or libraries in
  [Libraries.dev](https://github.com/Jakubantalik/Libraries.dev). Use the
  shared `libraries-dev` skill when one of its effects fits the user journey.
- For web motion, use [transitions.dev](https://transitions.dev) as a visual
  reference and match patterns to the project's motion tokens. Do not copy its
  code snippets unless the applicable license is clear; preserve reduced-motion
  behavior and test the interaction in the target browser.
- Before adding a dependency, verify framework/platform support, license,
  maintenance, accessibility, reduced-motion behavior, and runtime cost. Ask
  before installing a UI package unless the user already asked for installation.
- Do not bring a React or SwiftUI package into Flutter by analogy. Reuse the
  product's components and tokens, and adopt only a concrete pattern that
  improves the user's task.
- Avoid decorative effects that compete with content or undermine
  accessibility, reduced motion, or performance.

## Apple developer documentation

When reading Apple developer documentation, try the Markdown endpoint for `/documentation/` pages by appending `.md`. For Human Interface Guidelines and tutorials, use the `/tutorials/data/` route and a `.md` suffix; when a tutorial overview has no Markdown version, try `.json`. Source: https://gist.github.com/timsneath/239b026c1a32320b29889ee35c094da4

## Android and Flutter development

- For native Android work, inspect the app's Kotlin, Gradle, Compose, and SDK versions first. Read only the matching official Android skills from `~/.agents/skills` (including adaptive, edge-to-edge, navigation, security, testing, and profiler guidance as relevant), and use the installed `android` CLI and Android documentation when they fit the task.
- For Dart or Flutter work, read the matching official `dart-*` and `flutter-*` skills from `~/.agents/skills`. Use the local Dart MCP tools when available. Respect the repository's pinned Flutter/Dart version and project tooling; do not upgrade the device-wide SDK to satisfy one project's version.
- Keep device and emulator setup project-scoped. Do not erase or slim an active simulator, accept Android SDK licenses, or download large SDK images/IDEs without an explicit request. Check available disk before large platform installs.

## Web and product design

- For new or substantially reshaped UI, use `frontend-design` to choose a specific visual direction. Use `impeccable` when the request involves shaping, critique, accessibility, responsive behavior, polish, or a design-system audit. Use `web-design-guidelines` for web UI and accessibility review.
- Use `vercel-react-best-practices` and `vercel-composition-patterns` only for React/Next.js work; use the React Native skill only for React Native. For Flutter or native UI, use platform-specific skills and components rather than porting framework patterns by analogy.
- Select the few skills that match the task; these are on-demand references, not a checklist to load every time. Keep the product's established design system, content, accessibility, keyboard use, responsive behavior, and reduced-motion preference in view.
- For SEO, page ranking, organic traffic, or visibility in AI assistants (GEO), use `seo-growth-loop`: real Search Console and analytics data only, the diff gate before any publish, and the user's approval for live changes.
- Use installed web-app testing tools only when the user asks for tests/verification or that is part of the requested outcome. Do not add or run tests otherwise.

## Global Graphify use

Graphify is available across this device in `~/.agents/skills/graphify` and the agent skill profiles. For substantial codebase navigation, architecture questions, or multi-file impact work, query an existing `graphify-out/graph.json` first. If a project has no graph and one will materially help, invoke the Graphify skill (`$graphify .` in Codex; `/graphify .` in Claude/Gemini) to build it. After code edits, refresh an existing code graph with `graphify update . --no-cluster`. Keep graph data inside its own repository; do not scan unrelated projects or the whole home directory.

## Global stack maintenance

- Use `rtk proxy ~/.agents/bin/agent-stack-doctor` for a read-only audit of global agent configuration, tools, Android readiness, and skill provenance. Add `--catalog` for catalog details.
- Before adding global skills, consult `~/.agents/SKILL-CATALOG.md`; verify the source, license, revision, and profile coverage.
- For repeatable browser checks in a JavaScript/TypeScript project, use `~/.agents/WEB-PLAYWRIGHT-SETUP.md` and `~/.agents/bin/web-playwright-init`. Keep Playwright and browser binaries project-local; use the helper's `--apply --install` only when setting up that project.
